stemMd: If x means a statement and ¬x its negation, which expression is false for every truth value of x?
explanationMd: A statement and its negation cannot both be true. Their conjunction is therefore false whether x is true or false. Each other expression is a tautology under classical two-valued logic.

distractorRationale.c: One of the two alternatives is always true.
distractorRationale.a: This negates a contradiction and is always true.
distractorRationale.e: This is another ordering of the always-true disjunction.
